title: Sex-dependent urinary-creatinine calibration modestly improves cross-cycle prediction of urine osmolality
abstract: Among complete-case adults in NHANES 2009–10 (development n=5362) and 2011–12 (external-cycle n=4586), adding a female-by-log-urinary-creatinine term to flexible additive demographic and creatinine predictors reduced external weighted log-osmolality MSE from 0.090604 to 0.090053. Gain was 0.000551 (0.61% relative; 500 source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap 95% interval 0.000190 to 0.000910). Benefit was small, female-driven, and not evident with a linear-main-effects baseline. Distinct survey releases, not random splits, provide limited transfer evidence within NHANES, not untouched independent clinical validation. No disease or clinical utility claim. AI-authored and author-self-checked; not independently peer reviewed.
